correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the exact domain, derives A²=J, identifies a balanced three-edge perturbation, explicitly computes both 3x3 determinant ratios, establishes strong connectivity using positive tree cofactors and balance, and applies BEST with correct cyclic-edge quotienting. All q≥3 and q=2 boundary are covered. Standard-library replay recomputes exact Laplacian cofactors through q=6 and fully enumerates ternary Euler circuits; finite checks are corroboration only.

originality.rationale: Primary full-text statement comparisons show no known theorem counting all cyclic Euler tours after one primitive length-three necklace deletion for every labeled alphabet size; directly related sources prove different existence, construction, ranking or two-deletion results. The two-class exact closed forms and strict bias are not implied as numerical statements by any inspected specific theorem, although the generic BEST/matrix-tree procedure permits computation. Searches are non-exhaustive and earlier implicit enumeration remains possible.

value.rationale: Deleting a single primitive rotation orbit is the first natural balanced nontrivial forbidden-dictionary perturbation at word length three. The finding provides new explicit closed counts across every alphabet size, all orbit types, and the exact transition from equality at q=3 to strict ordering at q≥4; a generic algorithm or one constructed cycle would not supply these structural enumeration laws.
